categories.name: Simple carbs
categories.when: 30 to 60 min before · halftime · between games
categories.note: Fresh, frozen, dried or freeze-dried. Fruit is the fastest clean fuel there is.

categories.name: Quick starches
categories.when: the in-between carbs · fine close to games and practices

categories.name: Complex carbs
categories.when: meals · night before · breakfast · recovery dinner
categories.note: Regular pasta, rice and bread are all fine. Growing athletes need these. Carbs are her fuel, not the enemy.

categories.name: Healthy fats
categories.when: at meals · light before games (they digest slowly)

categories.name: Fast-digesting protein
categories.when: close to practices and games · game mornings · the Wake-and-Fuel Formula
foods: Protein powder (in a smoothie or shake)

categories.name: Regular protein
categories.when: meals · recovery · longer gaps between games
categories.note: Chocolate milk = simple carb + protein in one. That's why it's the classic recovery drink.

categories.name: Veggies
categories.when: meals only · never pre-game or between games
categories.note: Veggies matter every day. They just slow digestion, so they sit out the game window.

cooler.item: Tangerines + easy fruit: grapes, watermelon, strawberries
Bars: granola, Z-bar, Clif, protein bar
Deli meat sandwiches, easy on the veggies
Water. More than you think. Her bottle too.
Hot or outdoor tournament? An electrolyte drink
The salt pinch (a little bag of sea salt in her sports bag)

recipes.name: The Wake-and-Fuel Pancake Bake
recipes.blurb: The pancake recipe behind the Wake-and-Fuel Formula: egg whites and protein powder (fast-digesting protein) + oatmeal, ready the moment she wakes up. Cut squares, refrigerate, microwave 30 seconds.
ingredients: ¾ cup cottage cheese or plain Greek yogurt (pumpkin or applesauce works too)
3 stevia packets (or any sweetener: monk fruit, coconut sugar, brown sugar, agave)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a food processor or blender, process all the ingredients except the chocolate chips until smooth.
Grease an 8×11 baking dish with coconut oil or olive oil (spray is fine).
Fold in the chocolate chips, or whatever flavor you're doing.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Team Breakfast Baked Oatmeal
ingredients: ¼ cup strawberries + ¼ cup blueberries
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Grease a casserole dish with a little coconut oil (spray is fine).
In a large bowl, mix the oats, coconut sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and protein powder.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk, egg, oil and vanilla.
Line the dish with the sliced banana and half the berries, then spread the oat mixture over the fruit.
Pour the wet ingredients over everything so it's completely covered.
Top with the remaining berries and the walnuts, and sprinkle with a little more cinnamon.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.

recipes.name: Oatmeal Breakfast To-Go
recipes.blurb: Cut into bars and they ride in the backpack or the game-day bag. Oats + chia + protein powder: a bridge snack disguised as a breakfast bar.
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla, coconut, maple or almond extract
Toppings or fillings, pick any: ¼ cup freeze-dried berries, ¼ cup chopped walnuts or sliced almonds, ¼ cup shredded coconut, ¼ cup chocolate or carob chips, ¼ cup fresh berries
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a bowl, mix all the dry ingredients (the first 5).
In a separate bowl, mix the wet ingredients (banana through applesauce).
Mix the dry into the wet and combine well.
Fold in any of the topping or filling ingredients, use them just as topping, or both.
Bake for about 30 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Athlete Breakfast Cookies
recipes.blurb: A cookie she can eat in the car on the way to school or practice: oats, fruit, healthy fats, and protein if you add the powder. This is what "a treat that's secretly fuel" means.
ingredients: ½ cup almond or peanut butter
¼ cup or more chocolate chips
Optional: 2½ tbsp freeze-dried raspberries, or 2 tbsp dried fruit, or more chocolate chips
Optional: 2 tbsp sugar, or a pinch of stevia or monk fruit
Optional add-ins: chia seeds or hemp seeds (they won't taste them)
steps: Mash the banana with the applesauce, then mix in the nut butter and vanilla. Mix well.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Fold in the chocolate chips or other toppings.
Place on a cookie sheet with a mini cookie scoop or a tablespoon.
Bake at 350°F for about 15 minutes.
Makes about 20 to 24 cookies.

recipes.name: Strawberry Bridge-Snack Muffins
ingredients: 3 to 4 packets of stevia, to your taste
1 cup strawberries: half inside the batter, half for the top
Almond milk (¼ cup or so), added to the blender as needed
½ cup almonds or walnuts (optional), for crunch and healthy fats
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and spray a muffin pan (silicone works best) with coconut oil spray, then wipe down.
Place all the ingredients except the strawberries in a blender or food processor and blend until the oats are smooth.
Fold in half the strawberries.
Pour into the muffin pan and top with the remaining strawberries.
Bake for about 20 minutes, or until golden brown and done.

recipes.name: Blueberry-Chip Game-Day Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Mix all the ingredients in a bowl except the chocolate chips and blueberries.
Mix well, then fold in the berries and chips.
Pour into a muffin pan lined with coconut oil or avocado oil and bake about 20 to 25 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Mini Pumpkin-Chip Protein Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spray a 24-count mini muffin pan with coconut oil spray. Beat the eggs and add in the rest of the ingredients except the coconut flakes and chocolate chips.
Mix well, then fold in the coconut flakes and chocolate chips.
Pour the batter into the muffin pan and bake for about 25 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Banana Power Cookies
recipes.blurb: Use chocolate protein powder and these turn double-chocolate. Banana + oats + protein: a cookie that works as the evening snack from Is She Eating Enough?
ingredients: 2 scoops chocolate or vanilla protein powder
¼ cup almond milk or any milk
¼ to ⅓ cup chocolate chips (dairy-free works)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a bowl, mix the bananas, milk, almond butter and vanilla extract.
Add in the oats, protein powder and stevia and mix well.
Fold in the chocolate chips and dollop onto a parchment-lined cookie sheet.
Bake for about 14 minutes.

recipes.name: Blueberry-Chip Recovery Cookies
ingredients: 1 tbsp agave nectar, or monk fruit, coconut sugar or brown sugar
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a small saucepan, cook the berries until soft and syrupy.
In a food processor, blend all the ingredients except the chocolate chips.
Pour in the blueberries once softened, and blend again until smooth.
Fold in the chocolate chips and place spoonfuls on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Coffee Cake Banana Protein Bread
ingredients: Topping: 4 tbsp coconut oil (room temp), 2 tbsp coconut or brown sugar, 2 tbsp almond flour, 1 tsp cinnamon, ¼ cup chopped pecans
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a loaf pan.
In a bowl, mix all the wet ingredients and mix well.
Add in all the dry ingredients and mix well.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour the batter into the loaf pan.
In a small bowl, mix all the topping ingredients and spread over the batter.
Bake for about 45 minutes or until done.

recipes.name: Sloppy Turkey Bowls
recipes.blurb: Regular protein + complex carb, with finely chopped mushrooms and onions hiding in plain sight: the veggie-hiding system from The Picky-Eater Playbook, running at dinner.
steps: In a deep skillet, heat the cooking spray and add the garlic and onion.
Cook until soft, and add the mushrooms.
Once browned, add the turkey and cook, breaking it up until browned.
Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the sherry and cook, scraping the bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in the tomato sauce and Worcestershire and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Make the brown rice.
To serve, place the rice in a bowl, add the sloppy turkey on top, and finish with shavings of manchego. It's to die for.

recipes.name: The Fridge Meatballs
recipes.blurb: A whole package of spinach disappears into these. Double the batch: they hold in the fridge all week as grab-and-go regular protein, and they ride in the cooler for drive-distance tournaments.
ingredients: ¾ cup low-fat or fat-free mozzarella, shredded (optional)
1 tsp each of dried basil and oregano, or Italian seasoning
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a cookie sheet with foil.
In a large bowl, combine the egg, yogurt, mozzarella, Parmesan, garlic powder, seasoning and pepper.
Stir in the spinach.
Add the ground turkey and mix well.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs and place them on the cookie sheet.
Bake about 20 minutes or until the meatballs are no longer pink.

recipes.name: Hidden-Spinach Turkey Burgers
recipes.blurb: Serve on a bun (complex carb) with avocado (healthy fat) and dinner builds itself. These also batch and pack for tournament weekends, same as the meatballs.
ingredients: 1 tsp each onion and garlic powder
1 package frozen spinach, thawed (squeeze the water out)
steps: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl.
Form into patties.
Grill as usual.
